//: TASK-S2-O4 (2026-09-24, measured at 4e4e46f). A one-way ratchet over source sites that use a Node API newer than the repository's OWN declared floor. `engines.node` is `^20.19.0 || >=22.13.0` and `.nvmrc` is `20.19.0`, so the floor a consumer's engine check reads is 20.19.0 -- and two files use `fs.globSync`, which is `@since v22.0.0`. On the declared floor those files do not run at all: `node -e "console.log(typeof require('node:fs').globSync)"` prints `undefined` under v20.19.0 and `function` under v24.14.1, measured on both. That is the 08-11 finding H4 verbatim -- a documented gate that cannot start under the repository's own declared runtime -- and it is the reason the `validate-min-runtime` CI lane cannot be green while the floor says 20.
//why-not-fixed-here: The floor itself is OPEN OWNER DECISION D160 / D176 / `N5-04 D3` (register row 19): either raise `engines.node` to `>=22.13.0`, or keep the range and replace both `globSync` imports. TASK-R1-O4's `<stop_conditions>` named it an ADR-18 amendment rather than a fix, and this task inherits that boundary. What is in scope is stopping the breach set from GROWING while the decision is open, and making the next one visible in review instead of discovered by a red CI lane.
//how-it-ratchets: `maxBreaches` must EQUAL `breaches.length`, the same two-way handshake capability-matrix-ceilings.json and visual-baselines-ceilings.json use. A new site fails because it is unlisted. A repaired site fails because its entry is discharged and the ceiling must be lowered in the same change. Neither direction can be absorbed silently.
